evidence.title: Increased trust does not significantly increase willingness to follow the robot in one test
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: In the 2017 extension’s repeated task, greater reported trust did not yield the predicted significant increase in willingness to follow the robot (47% to 53%, p=.518). The repeated task comprised two parts of two trials; it was not a months-long study.
evidence.evidence_standing: Source-reported bounded account; study or measurement; not independently reproduced
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative or qualifying; does not validate a definition
evidence.limitations: Short controlled task and selected model/reward structure. A nonsignificant contrast does not establish equivalence or disprove all trust–adaptation mechanisms. Same programme and source family as the original robotics result, not independent replication.
evidence.open_questions: Transfer to other populations, tasks and operating environments remains unestablished. Missing measurement details are not inferred.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: retain an unsuccessful mechanism expectation rather than assuming trust necessarily produces adaptation.
evidence.dispute_status: See source version and dispute qualifications; no systematic clearance claimed.
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: Human–AI mutual adaptation
terms.definition: Reciprocal changes in human practices and AI-enabled activities as each responds to the other. Delegation can change how people decide and work; human behavior and institutions can reshape AI adoption, incentives, and subsequent capabilities.

terms.name: Mechanism hypothesis
terms.definition: A provisional explanation specifying how certain conditions, activities, or relationships could produce an observed or anticipated effect. A useful hypothesis names evidence that could support, qualify, or weaken the explanation.

relationships.explanation: A predicted trust-to-adaptation pathway was not statistically supported in this bounded test; other mechanisms remain possible.
Retains the unsuccessful trust-related expectation alongside the reciprocal-adjustment finding in the same programme.
